title: A typical Southern Syncopated Orchestra program at Philharmonic Hall
summary: Collier reads out a typical program with spirituals, rags, Cook compositions and Bechet's 'Characteristic Blues,' which Briggs confirms was typical.

blocks.x: Now, we also have another program, we want to put onto the record, which I have in my pocket. This is a concert given by the Southern Syncopated Orchestra, and this was their regular program, so this isn't dated. But these were when they were playing in Philharmonic Hall on Great Portland Street in London. Programs at 2:45 and 8:30. The orchestra, of course, is under the direction of Will Marion Cook. And in this particular program, the songs were 'Swing Along', which is one of Cook's songs, 'Hungarian Dance, No. 5,'

by Brahms. A medley of traditional tunes, "Go Down Moses", "Jesamin" and "Good News", Double Quartet, "Call of the Woods," -- that was the double quartet. Then there was an orchestral piece, "Call of the Woods," I see. Then there was a solo, "Swanee River" by Miss Lottie Gee..

Then a plantation medley by the orchestra. Then, "I Gotta Robe", which again would have been a spiritual, sung by Carol Morgan. "Ramshackle Rag," by the orchestra. "Listen to the Lambs," of course a famous concert piece, by MRS H.K. Rieves, who was singing it, that is to say. "Exhortation" by Joe Porter. That was written by Will Marion Cook. Porter was obviously the singer --
and the quartet, doing "Mammy of Mine", which is by Maclo Pinkard.
Then the orchestra did "Swanee Ripples." That was a rag, I suppose?
Then after the end of double quartet to "Deep River", and the orchestra did "Moanin' Trombone", which is a trombone specialty piece.
Joe Caulk sang "Mammy". The orchestra played "Russian Rag". Then a quartet did again a medley of "Mother of Mine", "Me, Oh Lord", and "Peaches Down In Georgia".
The orchestra played "Humoresque" and "Admiration". Then Miss Gee sang "Little Gal". Henry Saparo sang "Dixieland in France".

And then, obviously one of the high points of the program at that time, as I remember, Sidney Bechet played "Characteristic Blues", as a clarinet solo and accompanied by the orchestra, playing, I suppose, just

And then the Jubilee Quartet, sang "Tishomingo Blues", which I always thought was a Duke Ellington tune, but obviously is not, and "Jadda". Then there was an orchestral piece, "'Mid the Pyramids", and then the program was concluded by Will Marion Cook's composition, "Rain Song", played also by the orchestra. This program would have been very typical of the kind of thing it did --
